Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
255 AM EDT Tue Aug 25 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 253 AM EDT Tuesday...

No significant changes to the current forecast.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 253 AM EDT Tuesday...

1. Additional showers expected today as surface and upper level
troughs move across the area.

2. A dry and seasonable weekend will trend showery and more 
humid by early next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 253 AM EDT Tuesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: More shower activity is expected today as a 
surface trough and upper level trough both cross our area. Not 
expecting any thunderstorms or severe weather. Coverage and 
intensity should be less than yesterday. Winds will become more 
northwesterly as the day goes on as trough axis pushes east of 
our forecast area. Drier air will then work into the region, and
remain through Wednesday night with surface and upper level 
ridges building over the area. More shower activity is expected 
on Thursday into Thursday night, and lingering into Friday as 
well. A surface cold front along with some upper level shortwave
energy will cross the region.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Following a frontal passage and parent low 
departure Thursday and Friday, the weekend looks to trend drier 
as our flow pattern becomes more zonal. There still looks to be 
some signs of subtle cyclonic flow as the upper low lifts north 
and east, which may spur some isolated shower activity in 
eastern Ontario. Some of which could bring some increase cloud 
cover and an isolated shower to the St. Lawrence Valley (though 
PoPs are still below 20%). Temperatures will generally be 
seasonable in the 70s, though a few spot low 80s will be 
possible in the southern, wider valleys by Sunday. Humidity will
also gradually increase through the weekend from the upper 40s 
on Saturday to the upper 50s by Monday. The increase in humidity
will be a result of a trough swinging through the area to start
next week. Models diverge on the strength of this trough with 
the GFS ensembles denoting a continue more zonal pattern, 
whereas the Euro ensembles depict a slightly more amplified 
trough, which is in line with the CMC as well. The forecast will
likely change in the coming days as models resolve this feature
better in the days to come. As of right now, most of the area 
has a 30-40% chance for showers Monday, with temperatures in the
upper 70s which does seem to be on the warmer side of most 
guidance. There is a good chance for conditions to be quite a 
bit cooler early next week should the pattern become more 
amplified with additional cloud cover and daytime precipitation.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TUESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
Through 06Z Wednesday...Showers associated with an eastward 
moving trough are moving through the region with MVFR cigs on 
the leading edge and IFR cigs across the St. Lawrence Valley. 
Most terminal reductions tonight will be due to low stratus and 
not fog, with the exception of MSS/MPV where fog in the Ottawa 
River Valley bodes confidence for some intermittent IFR fog at 
MSS from 06-11Z, and low trapped moisture in eastern Vermont may
lead to intermittent fog at MPV from 09-12Z. Have used TEMPO 
groups as cigs will likely bounce between IFR/low MVFR. Outside 
of the fog, low stratus will trend most sites outside of PBG 
towards MVFR cigs at least between 2000-3000 ft agl. Low stratus
will likely trend ceilings lower to 1000-2000ft agl at MSS/SLK,
as the base of the trough moves over northern New York through 
13-15Z. With diurnal mixing, ceilings may lift to 2500- 3500ft 
agl by 18Z, then perhaps all VFR beyond 21-23Z. Isolated to 
scattered showers will accompany these low ceilings, with only 
PROB30 confidence at this time for showers at a terminal. All 
sites will see VCSH this afternoon, but confidence of a shower 
moving over a terminal is only 30-40% at this time. 

As the trough moves through this morning, light and variable 
winds will turn to the west-northwest under 10 knots for all 
terminals. Winds shifts will occur between 12-15Z from west to 
east. Models denote the potential for a brief winds shift to the
east at PBG due to a lake breeze during the late morning hours,
however, the shift looks to be short lived and quickly 
overtaken by the prevailing northwesterlies. Winds trend calm 
and variable with a return of low stratus and potential fog 
towards 06Z tomorrow night at the climatologically favored 
terminals.

Outlook...

Wednesday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Wednesday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Thursday: VFR. Chance SHRA, Chance TSRA.
Thursday Night: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. Chance
SHRA, Slight chance TSRA.
Friday: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Chance SHRA, Slight
chance TSRA.
Friday Night: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. Slight chance
SHRA.
Saturday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
